description: Structured eval definitions for the DynamoDB Table Deployer. Five-case proven set exercising the READY_TO_DEPLOY / PREREQUISITES_MISSING classification across workload types (session store, audit log, ad-tech ingest, cold archive) and missing-prerequisite branches. Each eval maps to a prompt file and a baseline (no-skill) file for with-skill-vs-baseline comparison.

eval_cases.name: Bursty session store with KEYS_ONLY GSI + TTL + Streams + on-demand
eval_cases.branch: READY_TO_DEPLOY — all checklist items verified, on-demand + customer CMK + PITR + TTL + Streams
eval_cases.prompt: Provision a production DynamoDB table named "prod-sessions" in us-east-1 for a high-throughput session store. Session IDs are UUID v4. We need a GSI to look up sessions by userId (most sessions have one, some anonymous sessions do not). Use SSE-KMS with customer-managed CMK alias/prod-dynamodb-key. Sessions expire after 24 hours via TTL on the "expiresAt" attribute. Enable DynamoDB Streams with NEW_AND_OLD_IMAGES — a downstream Lambda publishes session-change events. Traffic is bursty and unpredictable. Tags: Environment=production, Workload=session-store. Account ID: 123456789012.
eval_cases.expected_output:
TABLE: prod-sessions
VERDICT: READY_TO_DEPLOY
CHECKLIST:
  [✓] Partition key: sessionId (String) — UUID v4, high-cardinality for even write distribution
  [✓] Sort key: None (single-item lookup pattern)
  [✓] GSIs: gsi_by_userId (userId→sessionId, KEYS_ONLY projection, sparse — only items with userId)
  [✓] Capacity mode: PAY_PER_REQUEST (bursty session traffic, unpredictable peaks)
  [✓] Encryption: SSE-KMS customer CMK (alias/prod-dynamodb-key)
  [✓] PITR: Enabled (35-day window)
  [✓] TTL: Enabled (attribute: expiresAt — session token expiry, ~48h deletion lag acceptable)
  [✓] Streams: NEW_AND_OLD_IMAGES (downstream Lambda publishes session-change events)
  [✓] Table class: STANDARD (frequently accessed)
  [✓] Deletion protection: Enabled
VERIFICATION_COMMANDS:
  aws dynamodb describe-table --table-name prod-sessions
  aws dynamodb describe-continuous-backups --table-name prod-sessions
  aws dynamodb describe-time-to-live --table-name prod-sessions
  aws kms describe-key --key-id alias/prod-dynamodb-key

eval_cases.name: Compliance audit log with provisioned + autoscaling + no TTL (immutable)
eval_cases.branch: READY_TO_DEPLOY — audit log with provisioned capacity, no TTL (immutable retention), no Streams
eval_cases.prompt: Provision a DynamoDB table for compliance audit logging in us-east-1. Table name: "audit-events-prod". Workload is steady high-throughput (10k events/sec sustained, predictable). Use provisioned capacity with autoscaling. Use SSE-KMS with customer-managed CMK alias/audit-kms-key. Items must NEVER expire (regulatory retention). No downstream CDC consumer — Streams not needed. Use a composite partition key (tenantId + yyyy-mm bucket) with eventId as sort key. Deletion protection on. Tags: Environment=production, Workload=audit-log, DataClassification=confidential. Account ID: 123456789012.
eval_cases.expected_output:
TABLE: audit-events-prod
VERDICT: READY_TO_DEPLOY
CHECKLIST:
  [✓] Partition key: tenantId#yyyy-mm (String) — composite key for even distribution + tenant locality
  [✓] Sort key: eventId (String) — intra-bucket ordering
  [✓] GSIs: None (single access pattern via composite key)
  [✓] Capacity mode: PROVISIONED (steady high-throughput) with autoscaling on table (TargetValue=70)
  [✓] Encryption: SSE-KMS customer CMK (alias/audit-kms-key)
  [✓] PITR: Enabled (35-day window — supplements immutable log)
  [✓] TTL: Disabled (immutable audit log — regulatory retention; never auto-expire)
  [✓] Streams: Disabled (no downstream CDC consumer)
  [✓] Table class: STANDARD (sustained write workload)
  [✓] Deletion protection: Enabled
VERIFICATION_COMMANDS:
  aws dynamodb describe-table --table-name audit-events-prod
  aws application-autoscaling describe-scaling-policies --service-namespace dynamodb --resource-id table/audit-events-prod
  aws dynamodb describe-continuous-backups --table-name audit-events-prod
  aws kms describe-key --key-id alias/audit-kms-key

eval_cases.name: Operator has not specified partition key design nor CMK ARN — missing prerequisites
eval_cases.branch: PREREQUISITES_MISSING — partition key design and CMK ARN both unspecified
eval_cases.prompt: Help me create a new DynamoDB table called "orders-prod" in us-east-1. It needs SSE-KMS encryption. We will store order data — I think orderId should be the key but not sure about distribution. Region: us-east-1, Account: 123456789012.
eval_cases.expected_output:
TABLE: orders-prod
VERDICT: PREREQUISITES_MISSING
CHECKLIST:
  [✗] Partition key: NOT specified — orderId cardinality and write distribution unverified (hot-partition risk if sequential)
  [✗] Encryption: SSE-KMS requested but CMK ARN/alias not provided
VERIFICATION_COMMANDS:
  aws kms list-aliases --query 'Aliases[?starts_with(AliasName, `alias/`)]'
  aws sts get-caller-identity

eval_cases.name: Ad-tech event ingest with sparse INCLUDE GSI + Streams for OpenSearch zero-ETL
eval_cases.branch: READY_TO_DEPLOY — ad-tech ingest with sparse GSI (INCLUDE projection) + Streams for OpenSearch zero-ETL
eval_cases.prompt: Provision a DynamoDB table named "ad-events-prod" in us-east-1 for real-time ad-tech event ingest. Events arrive at 50k/sec, bursty. Partition key: adId (high cardinality). Sort key: eventTimestamp (ISO 8601 — for time-range queries). Need a sparse GSI "gsi_unprocessed_events" with partitionKey=status ("PENDING"), sortKey=eventTimestamp, INCLUDE projection on "bidAmount" and "advertiserId" attributes. TTL on "expiresAt" attribute (events expire after 7 days). Streams NEW_AND_OLD_IMAGES for OpenSearch zero-ETL indexing. SSE-KMS with customer CMK alias/adtech-kms-key. PITR on. Tags: Environment=production, Workload=ad-tech. Account ID: 123456789012.
eval_cases.expected_output:
TABLE: ad-events-prod
VERDICT: READY_TO_DEPLOY
CHECKLIST:
  [✓] Partition key: adId (String) — high cardinality for even write distribution at 50k/sec
  [✓] Sort key: eventTimestamp (String, ISO 8601) — enables time-range queries within an ad
  [✓] GSIs: gsi_unprocessed_events (status→eventTimestamp, INCLUDE projection on bidAmount,advertiserId, sparse — only PENDING items)
  [✓] Capacity mode: PAY_PER_REQUEST (50k/sec bursty traffic — on-demand handles spikes within burst bucket)
  [✓] Encryption: SSE-KMS customer CMK (alias/adtech-kms-key)
  [✓] PITR: Enabled
  [✓] TTL: Enabled (attribute: expiresAt — 7-day retention; ~48h deletion lag acceptable)
  [✓] Streams: NEW_AND_OLD_IMAGES (downstream OpenSearch zero-ETL indexing requires both images)
  [✓] Table class: STANDARD (high-throughput active workload)
  [✓] Deletion protection: Enabled
VERIFICATION_COMMANDS:
  aws dynamodb describe-table --table-name ad-events-prod
  aws dynamodb describe-continuous-backups --table-name ad-events-prod
  aws dynamodb describe-time-to-live --table-name ad-events-prod
  aws kms describe-key --key-id alias/adtech-kms-key

eval_cases.name: Cost-optimized cold archive on Standard-IA table class
eval_cases.branch: READY_TO_DEPLOY — cold archive on Standard-IA, TTL for 3-year retention
eval_cases.prompt: Provision a DynamoDB table named "historical-orders-archive" in us-east-1 for archived order data (3-year retention). Traffic is very low (a few queries per week from BI). Use the most cost-effective table class. Items DO expire at 3 years via TTL on "retainUntil". Use SSE-KMS with customer CMK alias/archive-kms-key. No GSI needed (single access pattern by orderId). PITR on for safety. Deletion protection on. Tags: Environment=production, Workload=archive. Account ID: 123456789012.
eval_cases.expected_output:
TABLE: historical-orders-archive
VERDICT: READY_TO_DEPLOY
CHECKLIST:
  [✓] Partition key: orderId (String) — low query volume, no hot-partition risk
  [✓] Sort key: None (single-item lookup pattern)
  [✓] GSIs: None (single access pattern)
  [✓] Capacity mode: PAY_PER_REQUEST (very low traffic — pay-per-request is cheaper than provisioned minimums for infrequent access)
  [✓] Encryption: SSE-KMS customer CMK (alias/archive-kms-key)
  [✓] PITR: Enabled
  [✓] TTL: Enabled (attribute: retainUntil — 3-year regulatory retention)
  [✓] Streams: Disabled (no CDC consumer)
  [✓] Table class: STANDARD_INFREQUENT_ACCESS (Standard-IA — lower storage cost for infrequent access)
  [✓] Deletion protection: Enabled
VERIFICATION_COMMANDS:
  aws dynamodb describe-table --table-name historical-orders-archive
  aws dynamodb describe-continuous-backups --table-name historical-orders-archive
  aws dynamodb describe-time-to-live --table-name historical-orders-archive
  aws kms describe-key --key-id alias/archive-kms-key
